rationale: Mara Voss, read as FIELD MEDIC in one second by stacking seven independent role cues down the figure: a pushed-up headlamp with a lit lens, bone collar piping, canvas apron bib-straps over the shoulders, a 10x10 bone cross stencilled on a rust chest bib, a bandolier of teal ampoules at the waist, a slung med-case her left hand is plunged into, and an oversized muzzle-up injector with a visible charge window clamped in her right fist. Proportions are 3.3 heads (head rows 2-19 = 18px; figure rows 2-61 = 60px) with a 20px-wide head, thin limbs and deliberately huge mitten hands - chibi hero, not naturalistic. Palette is 24 colours anchored on plum-black #120b10, no magenta or chartreuse; rust livery + bone markings carry identity, teal is reserved for the injector charge and ampoules only. The decisive craft fix was a three-tier value plan after grayscale showed teal, skin, canvas and metal all landing near luminance 130 and turning the mid-body to mush: darks (ink/coat/boots/belt ~14-66), mids (rust/canvas-shadow ~85-110), lights (skin/canvas/bone ~132-229), alternating vertically so rust bib -> dark belt -> pale trousers -> dark boots each separate. Sacrifices: the frame is full at 48px wide, so there is very little breathing room - the injector sits at x1 and the satchel at x44, and interior negative space is limited to two 1px armpit slits rather than generous holes. Fine detail (dose ticks, buckle rivets, knuckle ridges, the satchel's small cross) is authored for the 1x-to-4x range and is wasted below that. The figure is also deliberately asymmetric and bottom-heavy, which suits a grounded, gritty read but makes it less suitable if the lineup needs a centred, symmetrical idle.
frontFacingCue: A fully lit front face plane with an explicit feature set - two 3px-wide ink eyes under a hard dark brow band, a 2px nose shadow, and a 4px mouth line - rendered in skin at luminance 132 against hair at 48, an 84-step separation that survives grayscale. It is framed top and bottom by two more front-only reads: a pale headlamp band (luminance 191) running straight across the brow with its lamp housing jutting out to the left, and a 4-row lit neck only 8px wide dropping out of a 20px head into 26px shoulders, so the head demonstrably clears the shoulder line under the top-down dimetric camera. Nothing rises above the shoulders except the head. The chest cross, the bib straps and both hands are all frontal-plane elements, so the torso confirms the same facing the face does - the rejected version failed precisely here, burying a tiny face inside a hood blob that was the same width as the body with no neck at all.
smallCheck: Honest verdict: it survives, but reduced to three signals. I rendered a nearest-neighbour 21x28 downscale and inspected it magnified. What holds: the head reads as a head with a discernible dark eye band and the bright headlamp stripe anchoring it; the neck notch still separates head from shoulders; the chest cross reads unmistakably as a cross and is the single strongest shape; the injector reads as a dark tube with a teal core; the two legs stay separate and the boots anchor. What is lost: every sub-detail dissolves - dose ticks, ampoule caps, buckle rivets, knuckle ridges, the stray hair strand and the worn stencil chips all become stray single pixels or vanish. The satchel degrades worst: it survives as a rust mass but its small bone cross becomes a light smudge that competes with the chest cross rather than reinforcing it, and the left hand merges into the bag. The 1px armpit gaps close entirely, so the silhouette goes solid. If ~28px is the shipping size I would cut the satchel's cross marking, drop the ampoule bandolier to a plain dark band, and hand-tune a dedicated small variant rather than downscale this one - a naive downscale wastes roughly half the authored detail.
